spec.name: project-creation
spec.title: Project creation
spec.summary: Two ways to start a new Altruist server: the `altruist` dotnet template and the `altruist create` command of the Altruist.CLI tool. Both give you the same ready-to-run project with Program.cs, config.yml, one WebSocket portal and one REST controller.
use: When you start a new Altruist server from nothing and want a project that runs at once.
When you want a known-good layout (Program.cs, config.yml, Portals/, Http/) to copy from.
When you want a short command to run the current project (`altruist run`, which calls `dotnet run`).
avoid: When you add Altruist to an existing .NET project, add the packages by hand and write config.yml yourself; see application.
When you need a game with rooms, combat or inventory, create the project first, then add those packages (see the gaming capabilities).
spec.example:
```bash
# Option 1: the dotnet template (installs once, then works offline)
dotnet new install Altruist.Templates
dotnet new altruist -n MyServer
cd MyServer
dotnet run

# Option 2: the CLI tool (installs the template for you if it is missing)
dotnet tool install -g Altruist.CLI
altruist create MyServer
cd MyServer
altruist run          # same as: dotnet run
```

The project name must start with a letter and may contain letters, digits, `_` and `.`.
The template creates `Program.cs` (`await AltruistApplication.Run(args);`), `config.yml`
(HTTP on 0.0.0.0:8080, a JSON WebSocket at `/ws`, an in-memory cache), `Portals/HelloPortal.cs`
and `Http/HelloController.cs`. It references the packages Altruist, Altruist.Boot, Altruist.Socket and Altruist.Web.

spec.name: configuration
spec.title: Configuration
spec.summary: Altruist is configured from YAML, not from builder code. `config.yml`, then `config.{environment}.yml`, then environment variables, then command-line arguments are merged (later wins), and attributes pull the values into your classes. The same attributes can also switch whole services on or off.
use: When a value (port, rate, key, provider) should come from config.yml instead of being hard-coded; use `[AppConfigValue]` on a constructor parameter.
When a group of related settings belongs in one typed object; use `[ConfigurationProperties]`.
When a value must change while the server runs (tunables); use `ILiveConfigValue<T>`.

When a service should exist only if a config key is set, a package is installed, or no other implementation is registered; use `[ConditionalOnConfig]`, `[ConditionalOnAssembly]` or `[ConditionalOnMissingService]`.
When you need one instance per entry of a YAML list (for example one per world); use a list-mode `[ConditionalOnConfig(path, KeyField = "id")]` with `*:` paths.
avoid: When you only need to register a service without any settings, use `[Service]`; see services-and-modules.
When a value is a secret, keep it out of the committed YAML and set it by environment variable or `${NAME}` placeholder.
When you need the settings of one specific system (email, security, rooms), read that capability's config keys instead of the general mechanics here.

keyTypes.summary: Typed snapshot of the whole `altruist` configuration section, bound once at startup via `ConfigurationPropertiesAttribute` and injectable as a singleton (only if the section exists).
Snapshot of `altruist:server`: the HTTP listener and the transport section.
Snapshot of `altruist:server:http`, the keys the HTTP listener is started from. HTTP is hosted only when both `Host` and `Port` are set.
Snapshot of `altruist:server:transport`. Active transports are actually chosen by `altruist:server:transport:{tcp|udp|websocket}:enabled`.
Converts a config string to `Vector3`: `"x,y,z"` (e.g. `"0, 1.5, 0"`) or a JSON object `{"X":0,"Y":1.5,"Z":0}`. Blank input yields `Zero`.

Singleton service exposing the process's command-line arguments. Registered under its own type only (inject `ApplicationArgs`, not `IApplicationArgs`). To read arguments as configuration values use `AppConfigValueAttribute` instead.

Converts a config string to `Dictionary<string, string>`: a JSON object (`{"k":"v"}`) or `key=value` pairs separated by `,` or `;` (keys/values trimmed; pairs without a key or value are dropped; later duplicates win). Blank input yields an empty dictionary.
Converts a config string to `IEnumerable<string>` using the same rules as `ListStringConfigConverter` (JSON array or comma-separated).
Snapshot of `altruist:server:http`, the keys the HTTP listener is started from. HTTP is hosted only when both `Host` and `Port` are set.
Converts a config string to `List<string>`: a JSON array (`["a","b"]`) or a comma-separated list (`a, b`, entries trimmed, empty entries dropped). Blank input yields an empty list.
Converts a config string to `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>` using the same rules as `DictionaryStringStringConfigConverter` (JSON object or `k=v` pairs).
Converts a config string to `IReadOnlyList<string>` using the same rules as `ListStringConfigConverter` (JSON array or comma-separated).
Snapshot of `altruist:server`: the HTTP listener and the transport section.
Snapshot of `altruist:server:transport`. Active transports are actually chosen by `altruist:server:transport:{tcp|udp|websocket}:enabled`.
Converts a config string to `Vector2`: `"x,y"` (e.g. `"1.5, -2"`) or a JSON object `{"X":1.5,"Y":-2}`. Blank input yields `Zero`.
Converts a config string to `Vector3`: `"x,y,z"` (e.g. `"0, 1.5, 0"`) or a JSON object `{"X":0,"Y":1.5,"Z":0}`. Blank input yields `Zero`.

attributes.summary: Injects a configuration value into a constructor parameter, a `BeanAttribute` / `PostConstructAttribute` method parameter, or a public settable property (set right after construction) of a class built by the Altruist DI (`ServiceAttribute`, `ServiceConfigurationAttribute`, beans).
Marker for configuration classes implementing `IAltruistConfiguration`.

Registers the annotated `ServiceAttribute` class, MVC controller or portal only when the named assembly is loaded or loadable by the app (i.e. the package is referenced). Multiple attributes must all match.

Registers the annotated `ServiceAttribute` / `ServiceConfigurationAttribute` class only when configuration matches. Two modes: Gate (no `KeyField`): the class is registered only if the section at `Path` exists, or, when `HavingValue` is given, its value equals it (trimmed; case-insensitive unless `CaseInsensitive` is false). Multiple gate attributes must all match.List (`KeyField` set): `Path` points at a config list; one keyed instance is registered per item, keyed by the item's `KeyField` value, and constructed against that item's section (so `AppConfigValueAttribute` paths starting with `*`, e.g. `"*:gravity"`, read from the item). Every instance is also registered unkeyed, so `IEnumerable<T>` yields all of them. Only one list-style attribute per class is allowed; an item without the key field fails startup. Also used by `DependencyPlanner` when choosing implementations and by the missing-dependency diagnostics, which list the keys to add. Gate mode is additionally honoured for MVC controllers and portals (a gated-off controller or portal gets no route).

Registers the annotated class only when no other class registers `ServiceType`: a framework default that an application replaces by declaring its own `[Service(typeof(ServiceType))]`. Other classes that are themselves conditional on the same missing service, or whose `[ConditionalOnConfig]` does not match, do not count. A registration already present in the service collection when this class is processed (e.g. one added by hand or by a `BeanAttribute` method) also suppresses it.

Registers a custom string-to-type converter used by `AppConfigValueAttribute` conversion. The class must implement `IConfigConverter` (typically `IConfigConverter`); it is also registered as a singleton service under its own type.
Binds a plain configuration class (POCO) to the configuration section at `Path` once at startup and registers the bound instance as a singleton, so services can inject it as a typed settings object.

Marks a class implementing `IAltruistConfiguration` as a startup configuration step: it is registered in DI (constructor parameters, including `AppConfigValueAttribute` ones, are resolved like a service) and then its `Configure(IServiceCollection)` is called once, so it can add registrations by hand (options, authentication, hosted services, third-party integrations).

spec.name: services-and-modules
spec.title: Services, dependency injection and modules
spec.summary: Altruist finds your classes by attribute and wires them into the DI container, so you never write a Startup class. `[Service]` registers a class, `[ServiceConfiguration]` runs a step that adds registrations by hand, `[Bean]` registers a factory method, and `[AltruistModule]` runs one-time startup code once everything is built.
use: When you need an object you build by hand (a type you cannot annotate); use a `[Bean]` method.
When one-time startup work needs several services together (seeding a registry); use an `[AltruistModule]` static class with an `[AltruistModuleLoader]` method.
When a service needs initialization after the container is built, use a `[PostConstruct]` method.
avoid: When the setting is only a value or a section of YAML, use `[AppConfigValue]` or `[ConfigurationProperties]`; see configuration.
When you need a service locator in normal code, inject through the constructor. `Dependencies.Inject<T>()` is for static helpers only.
When your process needs no server (a worker or tool), use `AltruistDI.Run(args)` and not the full application; see application.

keyTypes.summary: Extension helpers on `IServiceProvider`.
A named framework service; the name identifies it in logs and health output.
A service backed by an external connection (database, cache, broker) whose availability gates server readiness.

Forwards packets to an external system (another server or broker). Used by the relay interceptor, which passes every decoded inbound packet to `Relay`. No built-in implementation is registered; provide one with `[Service(typeof(IRelayService))]` if you use relaying.
Token identifying the active transport backend.

Module-provided feature hookup. Takes the current builder 'stage' and returns the next stage. Examples: - AltruistIntermediateBuilder --(SetupGameEngine)--> AltruistConnectionBuilder - AltruistConnectionBuilder --(WithWebsocket)-----> IAfterConnectionBuilder

attributes.summary: Marks a type as an Altruist module. Must be applied to a public static class.

Marks a public static method of an `AltruistModuleAttribute` class as a module loader entrypoint. It must return `void` or a `Task` (awaited); every parameter is resolved from the root service provider (no `AppConfigValueAttribute` support; inject `IConfiguration` instead).

Marks a public (static or instance) method as a factory whose return value is registered as a DI service. Discovered at startup on every non-abstract class of the loaded assemblies by `AltruistDIServiceConfig` (bean methods are registered before `ServiceAttribute` classes).
Marks a portal method as the handler for an incoming packet event. Gate methods are registered when the framework warms up the portals at startup (see `PortalGateRegistry`).
Marks a class as a database keyspace/schema descriptor so the database module discovers and registers it. The class must be a concrete, non-abstract implementation of `IKeyspace`.

Tags a `PrefabModel` class with a stable identifier. A prefab is an in-memory aggregate of several related vault models (one root plus referenced components) that is loaded and saved together through `IPrefabs`; it has no table of its own.
Reserved component metadata for prefab properties (auto-load ordering and relation key).

Marks a one-to-one component owned by the root: a single `IVaultModel` whose foreign key points at the root's `StorageId`, so the key lives on the dependent row (e.g. a profile keyed by its account id). No nesting: Principal must be the root property name.
Marks a component reference that can be queried and included. No nesting: Principal must be the root property name.
Marks the root component (the FROM anchor) of a `PrefabModel`: the vault model every other component hangs off. Exactly one property per prefab must carry it.

Binds a `Portal` (realtime packet handler class) to a transport route. Portals are discovered by this attribute at startup, registered in DI automatically (no `[Service]` needed) and their `GateAttribute` methods are wired to incoming packet events.

Marks an initialization method that the framework calls once on each service instance after the root service provider has been built. Parameters are resolved like constructor parameters (DI services, `AppConfigValueAttribute`, `ServiceKeyAttribute`, collections).

Registers the annotated class in the DI container. At startup every non-abstract class carrying this attribute (in any loaded assembly) is discovered by `AltruistDIServiceConfig` and registered under its own type, plus a forwarding registration under `ServiceType` when one is given (both share the same instance for singletons). Constructor dependencies are planned and registered first (`DependencyPlanner`), and instances are built by `DependencyResolver`, which fills `AppConfigValueAttribute` / `ServiceKeyAttribute` parameters and properties.

Resolves a constructor, `BeanAttribute`-method or `PostConstructAttribute`-method parameter from a keyed service registration (keys come from `Name` or the item key of a list-style `ConditionalOnConfigAttribute`).

spec.name: application
spec.title: Application bootstrap and lifetime
spec.summary: `AltruistApplication.Run(args)` is the whole entry point of a server. It loads configuration, registers everything found by attribute, builds the container, runs modules, starts HTTP and the transports, and tracks readiness. Built-in health endpoints report the result.
use: When another part of the app needs to know whether the server is ready (database and cache connected); inject `IServerStatus`.
When a load balancer or Kubernetes probe needs a health check; use `GET /altruist/health` and check the `Online` field.
When a service connects to something external and should delay readiness until it is up; implement `IConnectable`.
avoid: When you need only the DI container, with no HTTP and no transports, use `AltruistDI.Run`; see services-and-modules.
When you want to change what the app does, do not edit bootstrap; add services, modules or config instead.

keyTypes.summary: Main entry point of an Altruist server application: loads configuration, registers everything discovered by attribute (services, beans, configuration steps, portals), runs `PostConstructAttribute` hooks and `AltruistModuleAttribute` modules, then starts the HTTP host and transports and blocks until shutdown.
The server bootstrap sequence behind `Run`. Call `Run` rather than this class directly; its members are public for custom hosts and tests.

Default `IAltruistContext`: process-wide server facts (address, portal endpoints, active transport / database / cache tokens) used for the startup banner and diagnostics. Singleton, registered by `ServiceAttribute`; inject `IAltruistContext`.
Process-wide description of the running server: address, registered endpoints, active backend tokens and process id.
The server's readiness state machine. Readiness is `Alive` only when every tracked `IConnectable` is connected; the game engine is started and stopped with it.

Tracks readiness from the connection state of every `IConnectable` service (the database and cache providers plus any registered `IConnectable`), and starts/stops the engine accordingly. Singleton; inject `IServerStatus`.
Describes the running server's public address: a display name plus the scheme, host and port clients connect to. Exposed as `ServerInfo` and in the health endpoint.
Built-in health endpoints at `altruist/health`: `GET` for a quick liveness/readiness probe and `GET details` for diagnostics (readiness, endpoints, dependency connection states).

services.summary: Altruist's `IHostApplicationLifetime` registration: three cancellation sources that are cancelled to signal started / stopping / stopped. The framework uses `StopApplication` to shut down when required services fail to connect at startup.

Default `IAltruistContext`: process-wide server facts (address, portal endpoints, active transport / database / cache tokens) used for the startup banner and diagnostics. Singleton, registered by `ServiceAttribute`; inject `IAltruistContext`.

Builds and runs the ASP.NET Core host for the server bootstrap: HTTP (controllers, authentication, readiness), WebSocket/TCP/UDP transports and portal routes. Started last by `Bootstrap`, after `PostConstructAttribute` hooks and modules.

Tracks readiness from the connection state of every `IConnectable` service (the database and cache providers plus any registered `IConnectable`), and starts/stops the engine accordingly. Singleton; inject `IServerStatus`.
Built-in health endpoints at `altruist/health`: `GET` for a quick liveness/readiness probe and `GET details` for diagnostics (readiness, endpoints, dependency connection states).

spec.name: server-engine
spec.title: Server engine and scheduling
spec.summary: The engine is the fixed-rate loop of the server: it runs recurring tasks, timers and effects every frame and applies state changes on one thread. Here live its contract (`IEngineCore`, `IAltruistEngine`), cron presets and the engine-aware router; the loop itself ships in Altruist.Gaming. It is not a web server and not a physics engine.
use: When game state is changed from a network or request thread and must be applied on the engine thread; use `WaitForNextTick` or `SyncCommit`.
When you need a one-shot timer (`ScheduleOnce`), a buff that repeats until it expires (`ScheduleEffect`) or slow I/O whose result the game needs (`RunOffTick`).
When work must run on the wall clock (daily reset, pruning); use `RegisterCronJob` with a `CronPresets` expression (UTC).
When you serialize work per entity; use `SendTask` with a stable `TaskIdentifier`.
avoid: When the code is plain request handling with no game loop, do not turn the engine on; leave `altruist:game:engine` out of config.
When you want a recurring method, mark it with the `[Cycle]` attribute; see the gaming capabilities.
When you want the game tick, world step and physics, see the Gaming Main capabilities; this capability only describes the shared contract.

keyTypes.summary: The game engine's fixed-rate frame loop and its schedulers. Registered as a singleton (`AltruistEngine`) when `altruist:game:engine` is configured; the loop runs at `altruist:game:engine:framerateHz` (alias `frequency`, default 30 Hz) on a dedicated engine thread once the server reports alive.

The engine API game code injects; same members as `IEngineCore` (see there for the frame phases and which scheduler to use). Registered as a singleton wrapper over the core engine when `altruist:game:engine:diagnostics` is `false` (pass-through) or `true` (times each task and logs throughput).

Names an engine task or effect. Equality is by `Id` (ordinal), so two identifiers with the same id refer to the same task: `SendTask` coalesces requests per id, and effect/timer handles returned by the scheduling methods are compared this way.

The engine-aware `IAltruistRouter`, registered when `altruist:game:engine` is configured. Same send API; its client sender defers sync packets to the engine loop. Inject `IAltruistRouter` unless you specifically need the engine variant.
Base router used when the game engine is configured. Uses `EngineClientSender`, so `Sync` packets sent to a client are delivered from the engine loop rather than inline.

Ready-made 5-field cron expressions (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) for `[Cycle("...")]` and `IEngineCore.RegisterCronJob`. Times are evaluated in UTC. Any other valid 5-field cron string works too; these are just named shortcuts.
Turns the `CronPresets` expressions into human-readable text (for logs and dashboards).

services.summary: `ClientSender` used with the game engine: packets whose `MessageCode` is `Sync` are sent from an engine task (`SendTask`, one unique task per send) and the call returns immediately; every other packet is sent exactly like `ClientSender`. Registered as a singleton when `altruist:game:engine` is configured.
Base router used when the game engine is configured. Uses `EngineClientSender`, so `Sync` packets sent to a client are delivered from the engine loop rather than inline.
Base router used when the game engine is configured. Uses `EngineClientSender`, so `Sync` packets sent to a client are delivered from the engine loop rather than inline.
The default `IAltruistEngineRouter` (single process). Inject `IAltruistRouter` rather than this type.

spec.name: email
spec.title: Email
spec.summary: Sends transactional email (verification links, password resets) through one interface, `IEmailSender`. A config key picks the provider: log it, Resend over HTTP, or any SMTP server.
use: When your game sends verification or reset emails; inject `IEmailSender` and call `SendAsync`.
avoid: When you send mail from a request handler, use `SendInBackground` so the caller never waits on the provider.
When you want marketing or bulk mail, use a dedicated mail service; this is for transactional messages.
When you hold a secret (API key, SMTP password), put it in an environment variable, not in a committed YAML file.

keyTypes.summary: Delivers transactional emails. Throws when delivery failed.
One transactional email: HTML plus a plain-text alternative.
`altruist:email`: which provider delivers transactional email and as whom.

The configured `IEmailSender`: `SmtpEmailSender` when `provider` is `smtp` with a host, `ResendEmailSender` when it is `resend` with an API key, otherwise `LogEmailSender` (with a warning for a `resend` / `smtp` that cannot send or an unknown provider).

Sends through any SMTP server with MailKit: one connection per email (connect, encrypt, authenticate, send, quit), a multipart/alternative message with the plain-text and HTML bodies of `EmailMessage`.
`altruist:email:smtp`: the SMTP server used when `altruist:email:provider` is `smtp`.
Fire-and-forget helpers for `IEmailSender`.

services.summary: The configured `IEmailSender`: `SmtpEmailSender` when `provider` is `smtp` with a host, `ResendEmailSender` when it is `resend` with an API key, otherwise `LogEmailSender` (with a warning for a `resend` / `smtp` that cannot send or an unknown provider).

spec.name: core-utilities
spec.title: Core utilities
spec.summary: Small helpers used across the framework and open to your code: a thread-safe pool for scratch collections, route and reflection helpers, and flag-enum helpers that do not mutate.
use: When a hot path (per tick, per packet) needs a temporary list, dictionary, set or StringBuilder; rent it from `AltruistPool` and return it in the same scope.
When you test, set or clear bits of a `[Flags]` enum without casting; use `FlagExtensions` (`IsSet`, `SetFlag`, `UnsetFlag`).
When you build a route from segments without double slashes; use `PathUtils.NormalizeRoute`.
avoid: When a collection is stored long-term, allocate it normally; pooling is only for short-lived scratch objects.
When you need pooled arrays, use `System.Buffers.ArrayPool<T>`.

keyTypes.summary: Centralized, thread-safe object pool for reusing expensive allocations. Eliminates per-system manual caching — any component can rent and return objects. Usage: var list = AltruistPool.RentList<int>(); list.Add(42); AltruistPool.ReturnList(list); // auto-cleared var dict = AltruistPool.RentDictionary<string, object?>(capacity: 16); AltruistPool.ReturnDictionary(dict); // auto-cleared All collections are cleared on return. Pool is bounded (default 64 per type).
Allocation-light helpers for `[Flags]` enums: test, set and clear bits without casting to integers.
Route/path string helpers shared by the transports and portal routing.

Small reflection helpers for mapping vault model types to storage columns (primary keys, clustering column, mappable properties, column names) honouring `VaultColumnAttribute`, `VaultIgnoreAttribute` and `VaultPrimaryKeyAttribute` across the inheritance chain.

spec.name: testing
spec.title: Testing
spec.summary: xUnit helpers that run your tests against the real Altruist container. `[AltruistTest]` builds a fresh DI container per test with mocks, `[AltruistIntegrationTest]` boots a real server for network tests, and `[AltruistE2ETest]` drives the client stack against a running server.
use: When you test a service with its real dependencies and want some replaced by mocks; use `[AltruistTest]` and `[Mock]` constructor parameters.
When you test TCP, UDP, WebSocket or HTTP round trips against a live server; use `[AltruistIntegrationTest]` with `TestTcpClient`, `TestWebSocketClient` and the like.
When you test the full client stack against a server that already runs (docker, staging) or from a host without xUnit; use `[AltruistE2ETest]` and `AltruistTestRunner`.
avoid: When a plain unit test needs no container, write a normal xUnit test.
When a test only checks business logic, prefer `[AltruistTest]`; it is faster and isolated per test than `[AltruistIntegrationTest]`.

keyTypes.summary: Custom xUnit v2 test framework. Classes marked `AltruistTestAttribute` are constructed via the Altruist DI container; all other classes use default xUnit behavior. Wire it once per test assembly: [assembly: Xunit.TestFramework("Altruist.Testing.AltruistTestFramework", "Altruist.Testing")] Then pick per class: `AltruistTestAttribute` (DI-resolved, per-class database schema, `MockAttribute` mocks), `AltruistIntegrationTestAttribute` (a live server booted in-process, test clients injected), or `[AltruistE2ETest]` with `AltruistE2EFixture` (client stack against an externally running server).

Process-wide root for test-time Altruist DI. Boot. Loads `config.yml` via the standard `AppConfigLoader`, then optionally overlays `config-test.yml` from the test assembly's base directory for any test-only overrides (logging, alternate connection strings, etc.). Bootstraps the full Altruist DI container — assembly scan, `[ConfigurationProperties]` bind, service registration, BuildServiceProvider, `[PostConstruct]`. `[AltruistModuleLoader]` runs lazily via `EnsureModulesRun` on first `[AltruistTest(RunModuleLoaders = true)]`. Database isolation. The configured persistence provider is used as-is — no automatic database rewrite. Per-class schema isolation lives in `AltruistClassRunner`: each test class gets its own schema (`test_<classname>`), purged-then-recreated at class start, dropped at class end (unless `[AltruistTest(KeepSchema = true)]`). Point `config.yml` at a test-suitable database; root bootstrap will create the production-named schemas there which serve as template structures for the per-class table clones.

High-level helper that drives the full new-player flow: signup → login → create-character → game/join → TCP connect → upgrade → enter-world. Exposes the resulting `Http` + `Tcp` clients so tests can keep driving them. public CombatTest(TestPlayerSession session) { _session = session; } public Task InitializeAsync() => _session.SetupPlayerAsync(race: 0); [Fact] public async Task Attacks() { await _session.Tcp.SendAsync("attack", new CAttack { VictimVID = 10001 }); } Each ctor param of `TestPlayerSession` gets its own pair of HTTP + TCP clients, so multi-player scenarios (party invite, exchange) just take two parameters. The endpoints invoked here come from Valeria's HTTP login surface (`/api/v1/auth/signup`, `/api/v1/auth/login/unamepwd`, `/api/v1/characters`, `/api/v1/game/join`, `/api/v1/auth/upgrade`). Other Altruist-based games using a different auth surface should drive the flow with raw `TestHttpClient` + `TestTcpClient` instead.

HTTP client pre-configured to talk to the Altruist test server. Inject one (or more) as a ctor parameter on an `[AltruistIntegrationTest]` class: public PartyTest(TestHttpClient http) { _http = http; } [Fact] public async Task Signup() => await _http.PostAsJsonAsync("/api/v1/auth/signup", new { username, email, password }); The base address is resolved from `altruist:server:http:host` and `altruist:server:http:port` (config.yml + config-test.yml overlay) at boot time. Wildcard binds (`0.0.0.0`, `*`, `+`) are rewritten to `localhost` for client-side use. Subclasses `HttpClient`, so all standard methods — `PostAsJsonAsync` (System.Net.Http.Json), `GetAsync`, etc. — are available with no adapter layer.

TCP client pre-configured to talk to the Altruist test server. Knows the Altruist wire framing — 4-byte little-endian length prefix, 1-byte event-name length, UTF-8 event name, codec-encoded payload — so tests don't reimplement it per file. public PartyTest(TestTcpClient tcp1, TestTcpClient tcp2) { _t1 = tcp1; _t2 = tcp2; } await _t1.ConnectAsync(); // reads server-assigned ClientId await _t1.SendAsync("enter-world", new CEnterGame()); var packets = await _t1.DrainAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1)); Each ctor param of type `TestTcpClient` gets its own instance — multi-client scenarios (party invites, exchange, PvP) just take two parameters. Endpoint resolution: `altruist:server:transport:tcp:host` / `altruist:server:transport:tcp:port`. Codec resolution: `altruist:server:transport:tcp:codec:provider` with fallback to `altruist:server:transport:codec:provider`. Wildcard binds rewrite to localhost.

Per-class fixture for `AltruistE2ETestAttribute` tests. Loads `config.yml` + an optional `config.E2E.yml` overlay once per test class, provides a single `ResetAsync` hook against the running server's `/e2e/v1/reset` endpoint, and factory-builds per-test `E2EClientStack` instances on demand. The fixture itself does not own a player session — each test gets its own `E2EClientStack` via `NewClientStack`, which owns one `TestPlayerSession`, one `ClientPacketDispatcher`, and one `ClientInventoryService`. Disposing the stack tears them all down. Server requirement. A real server must be running with `altruist:e2e:enabled=true` (typically the `docker-compose-e2e.yml` stack). Without the flag, `ResetAsync` returns 404. Test pattern: [AltruistE2ETest] public sealed class InventoryE2ESmokeTests : IClassFixture<AltruistE2EFixture> { readonly AltruistE2EFixture _e2e; public InventoryE2ESmokeTests(AltruistE2EFixture e2e) => _e2e = e2e; [Fact] public async Task Login_populates_bag() { await _e2e.ResetAsync(); await using var stack = _e2e.NewClientStack(); stack.Inventory.RegisterContainer(new GridLayout(1, 5, 9)); await stack.Session.SetupPlayerAsync(race: 0); await stack.PumpAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2)); Assert.NotNull(stack.Inventory.GetSnapshot(window: 1, cell: 0)); } }

Reflection-based test runner for `AltruistE2ETestAttribute` classes. Designed to run in any host that can load .NET reflection — server CLI, console app, or Unity Editor (where xUnit's own runner doesn't function). Server-side `dotnet test` still uses xUnit; this runner is for hosts where xUnit is unavailable. Discovery contract. A test is any public instance method marked `[Fact]` on a class marked `AltruistE2ETestAttribute`. Methods may return `void` or `Task`. Construction. Test classes are constructed via parameterless constructor. Optional `IAsyncLifetime` hooks (`InitializeAsync`/`DisposeAsync`) fire around each method. `IClassFixture<T>` is not implemented in this runner — server-side tests using one should run via `dotnet test`; Unity hosts should keep setup logic in the test class itself or use `IAsyncLifetime`. Concurrency. Tests run sequentially. Parallel execution is a future enhancement; sequential matches the shared-server model the E2E stack uses today.

attributes.summary: Marker on a test class that needs a real Altruist server (HTTP + transports) running for the duration of its `[Fact]`s. The framework boots a single process-shared server lazily on the first `[AltruistIntegrationTest]` class encountered, then keeps it alive until the test process exits. When to use this vs `AltruistTestAttribute`: reach for `[AltruistIntegrationTest]` only when the test exercises the network surface itself (TCP packet round-trip, HTTP signup/login, broadcast routing, multi-client visibility). For service-level assertions (vault writes, business logic), `[AltruistTest]` is faster and gives per-test isolation. Config. Boot uses `config.yml` + an optional `config-test.yml` overlay loaded from the test assembly's base directory. Override host/port/database/etc. there. Database. The configured persistence provider is used as-is — no per-class schema isolation in this mode (the live server's DI is bound to one schema for its whole lifetime). Tests must use unique IDs (Guid) to avoid colliding with parallel tests in the same assembly. Injection. Constructor parameters of type `TestHttpClient`, `TestTcpClient`, `TestUdpClient`, `TestWebSocketClient` and `TestPlayerSession` get a fresh instance each (per test case); any other parameter resolves from the live server's container. Opt into `Internal.AltruistTestCollectionFactory` to serialize integration classes against the shared server. [AltruistIntegrationTest] public sealed class EchoTests { private readonly TestTcpClient _tcp; public EchoTests(TestTcpClient tcp) => _tcp = tcp; [Fact] public async Task Echoes() { await _tcp.ConnectAsync(); await _tcp.SendAsync("echo", new { text = "hi" }); Assert.NotEmpty(await _tcp.DrainAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1))); } }

Marks a test class for resolution from the real Altruist DI container. Constructor parameters resolve from DI; parameters marked `MockAttribute` are substituted with Moq mocks visible to the rest of the per-class container. Requires the assembly to register the framework: `[assembly: Xunit.TestFramework("Altruist.Testing.AltruistTestFramework", "Altruist.Testing")]` Each `[Fact]` gets a freshly built container (cloned from `RootDescriptors`, fresh singletons and mocks) and every vault targets the class's own Postgres schema (`test_<classname>`). Use it for service-level tests (vault writes, business logic); use `AltruistIntegrationTestAttribute` when the test needs the network surface. [AltruistTest(RunModuleLoaders = false)] public sealed class ScoreServiceTests { private readonly IScoreService _scores; private readonly Mock<IClock> _clock; // IScoreService is built with the mocked IClock as its dependency. public ScoreServiceTests(IScoreService scores, [Mock] IClock clock) { _scores = scores; _clock = Mock.Get(clock); } [Fact] public async Task Adds_points() => Assert.Equal(10, await _scores.AddAsync("p1", 10)); }

Marks a test class as a client-side end-to-end test. Tests so marked drive the same Altruist client transport stack the Unity client uses (codec, dispatcher, mirror) against a real running server, instead of building a per-class DI scope like `[AltruistTest]` (Altruist.Testing). When to use.`[AltruistTest]` for service-level tests against the DI container (fast, per-class schema isolation); `[AltruistIntegrationTest]` to exercise the network surface against a server the test process boots itself; `[AltruistE2ETest]` to drive the client stack against an externally running server (docker stack, staging), from `dotnet test` or, through `AltruistTestRunner`, from hosts without xUnit (a game-engine editor, a console app). Setup contract. Tests are expected to take an `AltruistE2EFixture` via xUnit's `IClassFixture<AltruistE2EFixture>` (Altruist.Testing); the fixture loads `config.yml` + an optional `config.E2E.yml` overlay and builds per-test client stacks (`TestPlayerSession` with its `TestHttpClient`/`TestTcpClient`, a packet dispatcher, an inventory mirror) for the test to drive. Server requirement. A real server must be running and configured with `altruist:e2e:enabled=true`. The standard pattern is a dedicated `docker-compose-e2e.yml` stack with a separate Postgres database, so tests never touch production data. This attribute also adds a `Category=E2E` xUnit trait so test runs can opt-in or opt-out via `dotnet test --filter Category=E2E`.

Replaces a constructor parameter's service with a `Mock`.`Object` for one test method (each `[Fact]` gets a fresh mock in its freshly built container). The mock replaces every registration of the parameter's type BEFORE the provider is built, so other DI-resolved services in the same constructor see the mock as their dependency (Spring `@MockBean` behavior). Only on constructors of `AltruistTestAttribute` classes; get the `Mock` back with `Mock.Get(parameter)` to set it up.

spec.name: transports
spec.title: Transports and connections
spec.summary: The listeners that accept client connections: TCP, UDP and WebSocket, plus the connection manager that tracks every live connection. You turn each transport on in config.yml and any mix can run at once. Portal code stays the same on all of them.
use: When you need a browser client (WebSocket), a reliable desktop or mobile stream (TCP) or fast unreliable updates (UDP).
When you need to cap connections, set the idle timeout or change a port.
When you write a new kind of transport (implement ITransport) or need to look up or close a connection by id.
avoid: When you need to handle what clients send, use portals-and-routing instead. Transports only deliver bytes.
When you need to choose the message format (JSON or MessagePack), use packets-and-codecs instead.
When you need REST endpoints, use http-api instead.
spec.example:
```yaml
# config.yml: run WebSocket for browsers and TCP + UDP for desktop clients
altruist:
  server:
    transport:
      max-connections: 2000
      websocket:
        enabled: true
      tcp:
        enabled: true
        port: 13000
      udp:
        enabled: true
        port: 13001
```

```csharp
// Program.cs: nothing else is needed, the enabled transports start with the app
using Altruist;
await AltruistApplication.Run(args);
```

keyTypes.summary: A network transport (WebSocket, TCP, UDP) that accepts client connections and hands them to the `IConnectionManager`. Implementations register themselves with `[Service(typeof(ITransport))]` gated by `altruist:server:transport:<name>:enabled`; the startup pipeline iterates every registered transport.

Default `IConnectionManager` (singleton, registered when `altruist:server:transport` is configured). Transports hand every accepted connection to `HandleConnection`, which runs the portal lifecycle hooks, the read loop, interceptors and gate dispatch, and the disconnect path. Connection/room queries delegate to `ISocketManager`.

Owns the server side of every client connection: runs the read loop, dispatches packets to portal gates through the interceptors, fires portal connect/disconnect hooks, and exposes the connection/room registry (delegating to `ISocketManager` / `IConnectionStore`). Registered as a singleton when `altruist:server:transport` is configured.

Connection and room registry used by the networking layer: which client connections exist, and which room (group of connections) each one is in. Inject this to look up a client's `AltruistConnection` or the members of a room.

Raw TCP transport (`altruist:server:transport:tcp:enabled: true`). Listens on all interfaces at `altruist:server:transport:tcp:port` (13000) and hands each socket to `HandleConnection` with route `altruist:server:transport:tcp:event` (`/game`).

Experimental UDP transport (`altruist:server:transport:udp:enabled: true`), listening on `altruist:server:transport:udp:port` (13001) with route `altruist:server:transport:udp:event` (`/game`). Client ids are a Murmur3 hash of the sender's `ip:port`.

WebSocket transport that supports multiple routes (paths) but uses a single IConnectionManager instance for handling connections. Each route can specify an optional ShieldAttribute (authorization) which is enforced per-route.
Tracks TCP connection count, max limit, and login queue. Registered as a singleton service so HTTP controllers can query it.

services.summary: Default `IConnectionManager` (singleton, registered when `altruist:server:transport` is configured). Transports hand every accepted connection to `HandleConnection`, which runs the portal lifecycle hooks, the read loop, interceptors and gate dispatch, and the disconnect path. Connection/room queries delegate to `ISocketManager`.

Default `IConnectionGate` (singleton). `TcpTransport` calls `TryAdmit` per accepted socket and `Release` when it closes; the queue is maintained by the queue endpoints of `QueueStatusController` and is informational only (admission does not consult it).
Queue status endpoint — requires JWT authentication. Returns the caller's position in the login queue and estimated wait.
Public health endpoint — no auth required. Returns connection count, max, queue length, and server status.
Transport configuration registered when TCP is enabled; only logs activation.

Raw TCP transport (`altruist:server:transport:tcp:enabled: true`). Listens on all interfaces at `altruist:server:transport:tcp:port` (13000) and hands each socket to `HandleConnection` with route `altruist:server:transport:tcp:event` (`/game`).
Service token announcing the TCP transport (startup banner/registration).
Transport configuration registered when UDP is enabled; only logs activation.

Experimental UDP transport (`altruist:server:transport:udp:enabled: true`), listening on `altruist:server:transport:udp:port` (13001) with route `altruist:server:transport:udp:event` (`/game`). Client ids are a Murmur3 hash of the sender's `ip:port`.

Default `ISocketManager` (registered as a singleton service when `altruist:server:transport` is configured). Every member is virtual and simply delegates to the injected `IConnectionStore`; subclass it to add behaviour around connection/room changes.

WebSocket transport that supports multiple routes (paths) but uses a single IConnectionManager instance for handling connections. Each route can specify an optional ShieldAttribute (authorization) which is enforced per-route.

config.description: Set to `true` to turn Altruist.Socket.TcpSocketConfiguration on.
Route assigned to TCP connections (`tcp:event`, default `/game`).
Set to `true` to turn Altruist.Socket.UdpSocketConfiguration on.
Set to `true` to turn Altruist.Web.WebSocketTransportToken on.

spec.name: portals-and-routing
spec.title: Portals, gates and routing
spec.summary: A portal is a class that handles client messages. Each gate method on it handles one event name, and the router sends replies to one client, a room or everyone. Interceptors can inspect or drop packets before a gate runs, and an outbound queue can send without blocking your handler.
use: When you send a packet to one client, a room or all clients with IAltruistRouter.
When you need to react to a client connecting or disconnecting (OnConnectedAsync, OnDisconnectedAsync).
When you filter or log every incoming packet with an IInterceptor, or send through the queued outbound mode for busy game loops.
avoid: When you need to limit how fast a client may send, use rate-limit instead. It is built on interceptors.
When you only need to send entity changes (changed properties), use entity-sync instead.
When you serve plain request and response over HTTP, use http-api instead.

keyTypes.summary: Base class for realtime packet handlers. Annotate the subclass with `PortalAttribute` to bind it to a route, add `GateAttribute` methods to handle incoming packet events, and optionally implement `OnConnectingAsync`, `OnConnectedAsync` and `OnDisconnectedAsync` to observe the connection lifecycle.
Marker contract for a portal: a class that groups realtime packet handlers (`GateAttribute` methods) and connection lifecycle hooks for one transport route.
The main send API: one entry point with a sender per audience. Inject `IAltruistRouter` (singleton) in portals and services that push packets to clients.

Sends packets to one client. `SendAsync` encodes and awaits the socket (`altruist:server:transport:outbound:mode: direct`, the default) or hands the packet to the client's outbound queue and returns (`queued`). `Enqueue` and `CloseAfterFlush` always use the queue (see `OutboundQueues`): in order per client, never waiting on a socket, with `CoalesceAttribute` packets superseding each other and slow readers aborted.
Sends a packet to every connected member of a room, one `ClientSender` send per member, in sequence. Registered as a singleton when `altruist:server:transport` is configured; use it through `Room`.

Sends a packet to every connected client in the connection store, optionally excluding one. Registered as a singleton when `altruist:server:transport` is configured; use it through `Broadcast`. For a subset of clients use `RoomSender`.

Runs before every gate handler (all interceptors complete before the handler starts). An interceptor can veto the packet with `Reject`. Packets for unknown events are intercepted too (for rate limiting), with a null `eventData`. Register one as `[Service(typeof(IInterceptor))]` and the connection manager picks it up from DI; `AddInterceptor` still works for manual setup. Use `Route` to limit an interceptor to one portal.

Per-client outbound queues behind `Enqueue`, `CloseAfterFlush` and queued-mode sends. The caller only enqueues (it never encodes or waits on a socket); one pump per client drains that client's queue on the thread pool, in order, so a slow or stalled client cannot delay the caller or any other client. Packets marked `CoalesceAttribute` supersede queued packets with the same key.A client whose send has been in flight longer than `stuck-send-seconds`, or that has more than `max-queued-per-client` packets waiting, is not reading: its connection is aborted and the normal disconnect path runs. Both are checked when a packet is enqueued.Packets are encoded like `ClientSender` does (a `MessageEnvelope` stamped for the receiver), into a reused per-client buffer when the codec supports `IBufferEncoder`. One instance per process (every `ClientSender` resolved from DI shares it). Config: `altruist:server:transport:outbound:{mode,max-queued-per-client,stuck-send-seconds,encode-buffer-bytes}`.

services.summary: Sends a packet to every connected client in the connection store, optionally excluding one. Registered as a singleton when `altruist:server:transport` is configured; use it through `Broadcast`. For a subset of clients use `RoomSender`.

Sends packets to one client. `SendAsync` encodes and awaits the socket (`altruist:server:transport:outbound:mode: direct`, the default) or hands the packet to the client's outbound queue and returns (`queued`). `Enqueue` and `CloseAfterFlush` always use the queue (see `OutboundQueues`): in order per client, never waiting on a socket, with `CoalesceAttribute` packets superseding each other and slow readers aborted.

Per-client outbound queues behind `Enqueue`, `CloseAfterFlush` and queued-mode sends. The caller only enqueues (it never encodes or waits on a socket); one pump per client drains that client's queue on the thread pool, in order, so a slow or stalled client cannot delay the caller or any other client. Packets marked `CoalesceAttribute` supersede queued packets with the same key.A client whose send has been in flight longer than `stuck-send-seconds`, or that has more than `max-queued-per-client` packets waiting, is not reading: its connection is aborted and the normal disconnect path runs. Both are checked when a packet is enqueued.Packets are encoded like `ClientSender` does (a `MessageEnvelope` stamped for the receiver), into a reused per-client buffer when the codec supports `IBufferEncoder`. One instance per process (every `ClientSender` resolved from DI shares it). Config: `altruist:server:transport:outbound:{mode,max-queued-per-client,stuck-send-seconds,encode-buffer-bytes}`.
Sends a packet to every connected member of a room, one `ClientSender` send per member, in sequence. Registered as a singleton when `altruist:server:transport` is configured; use it through `Room`.

attributes.summary: Marks a packet type whose queued copies supersede each other: a client's outbound queue keeps at most one unsent packet per key (the newest, moved behind everything queued before it), so a client that reads slowly skips stale states instead of building a backlog. Typical use: world snapshots. Applies to `Enqueue` and to queued-mode sends.

spec.name: packets-and-codecs
spec.title: Packets and codecs
spec.summary: Packets are the typed messages sent between client and server, each with a numeric message code. Codecs turn them into bytes: JSON for browsers and debugging, MessagePack for compact binary. The Altruist.Protocol package holds the shared packet contracts, so other projects can use them without the server.
use: When you choose JSON or MessagePack for all transports or per transport.
When you need the built-in packets (handshake, text, success or failed results, sync) or the transport result codes.
When you add a new wire format by implementing ICodec and registering it with [CodecProvider].
avoid: When you handle a packet on the server, use portals-and-routing instead.
When you send many numeric rows every tick in a compact positional form, use snapshots instead.

keyTypes.summary: Contract every routable Altruist packet implements: a packet type identified on the wire by its `MessageCode`. Shared by server and client so both sides agree on the code-to-type mapping.
Marker interface for any model that is sent over the wire. Carries no members.

The inbound event envelope (`Altruist`): names the event a client sent so the connection manager can route it to the matching handler. JSON clients send `{"event": "name", "data": {...}}`; binary codecs use event-prefixed framing (`[1-byte length][UTF-8 event name][payload]`), from which the framework builds this packet.

Outer frame of every server-to-client message: a MessagePack fixarray(3) `[MessageCode, Header, Message]` (or the JSON object `{ "messageCode", "header", "message" }`). The code is duplicated at the front so receivers can route a frame without deserializing the inner packet.
A wire format for realtime packets: a matched `IEncoder`/`IDecoder` pair.

JSON wire format (provider name `json`). Human-readable and easy to consume from browsers; prefer `MessagePackCodec` (`messagepack`) for smaller, faster binary packets. Select it with `altruist:server:transport:codec:provider: json`.

MessagePack wire format (provider name `messagepack`): compact binary, hardened against hostile input via `MessagePackStructureGuard` and `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData`. The usual choice for game traffic; use `JsonCodec` (`json`) when clients need readable text. Select it with `altruist:server:transport:codec:provider: messagepack`.
Default `ICodecResolver`: collects DI-registered codecs plus every other `CodecProviderAttribute` type found by reflection (created with `ActivatorUtilities`) once, at construction.

services.summary: System.Text.Json decoder using the DI-registered `JsonSerializerOptions`. Registered as the standalone `IDecoder` singleton only when `altruist:server:transport:codec:provider` is `json`; normally reached through `JsonCodec`.

System.Text.Json encoder (UTF-8 bytes, runtime type of the message) using the DI-registered `JsonSerializerOptions`, the same options `JsonMessageDecoder` reads with, so property naming matches in both directions. Registered as the standalone `IEncoder` singleton only when `altruist:server:transport:codec:provider` is `json`; normally reached through `JsonCodec`.
Default `ICodecResolver`: collects DI-registered codecs plus every other `CodecProviderAttribute` type found by reflection (created with `ActivatorUtilities`) once, at construction.

config.description: Set to `json` to turn Altruist.Codec.JsonMessageDecoder on.

attributes.summary: Names a codec implementation so it can be selected via config. Example: [CodecProvider("json")] or [CodecProvider("messagepack")] Users can create custom codecs with any name: [CodecProvider("protobuf")]

spec.name: rate-limit
spec.title: Rate limiting for portals
spec.summary: A per-connection token-bucket limiter that runs before every gate handler. It drops packets that come too fast or are too large, and closes the connection of a client that keeps breaking the limits. It is installed from config.yml, with no code.
use: When clients can spam gates (chat, input, matchmaking) and you want hard limits per gate.
When you cap the payload size of incoming packets.
When you assign a gate to a bucket in code with [RateLimit("bucket")].
avoid: When you limit HTTP endpoints, use http-api instead. It has its own named policies (the same [RateLimit] attribute works there).
When you need custom per-packet logic that is not a rate, write an IInterceptor (see portals-and-routing).

keyTypes.summary: Applies the configured rate limits (`RateLimitOptions`) before every gate handler. Installed when `altruist:server:transport:rate-limit:enabled: true`; packets over a limit are rejected, and a connection with too many strikes is closed (its output side: the read loop then runs the normal disconnect path). Register your own `IRateLimiter` in DI to replace the token buckets.
Per-connection rate limiting; the default implementation is `TokenBucketRateLimiter`.

Token buckets per connection and bucket, as configured by `RateLimitOptions`. A gate's bucket comes from the bucket that lists it, else from its `RateLimitAttribute`, else the default bucket; a bucket name that is not configured is unlimited. Buckets start full.

`altruist:server:transport:rate-limit`: per-connection limits applied by `RateLimitInterceptor` before every gate handler (and to packets for unknown events). Each connection gets one token bucket per configured bucket; a packet takes one token from the bucket of its gate. A packet over its bucket, or larger than `MaxPayloadBytes`, is dropped and counts as a strike (an oversize one as `OversizeStrikes`); `StrikesToDisconnect` strikes within `StrikeWindowSeconds` close the connection.
Outcome of a rate-limit check.

Receives every rate-limit verdict of `RateLimitInterceptor`. Register an implementation in DI (`[Service(typeof(IRateLimitMetrics))]`); none is registered by default. Called on the connections' read loops: implementations must be thread-safe and cheap.

services.summary: Applies the configured rate limits (`RateLimitOptions`) before every gate handler. Installed when `altruist:server:transport:rate-limit:enabled: true`; packets over a limit are rejected, and a connection with too many strikes is closed (its output side: the read loop then runs the normal disconnect path). Register your own `IRateLimiter` in DI to replace the token buckets.

config.description: Set to `true` to turn Altruist.RateLimitInterceptor on.

attributes.summary: Names a rate limit. On a gate handler: its bucket (`altruist:server:transport:rate-limit:buckets:<name>`). A bucket that lists the gate in its `gates` takes precedence; gates in no bucket use the `default-bucket`.On an MVC controller or action: an HTTP policy (`altruist:server:http:rate-limit:policies:<name>`, see `HttpRateLimitOptions`); controller and action policies both apply.

spec.name: entity-sync
spec.title: Entity synchronization
spec.summary: Delta sync for world entities. Mark properties with [Synced] and the class with [Synchronized], and Altruist sends clients only the properties that changed, as a SyncPacket.
use: When world objects (players, NPCs) change a few properties per tick and clients should get only the changes.
When you send an entity's changes by hand with IAltruistRouter.Synchronize.
avoid: When you send positional numeric rows for many objects every tick, use snapshots instead.
When you send rare, mixed messages, use a normal packet (packets-and-codecs) instead.

keyTypes.summary: An object whose `SyncedAttribute` properties can be delta-synchronized to clients. Implement it on world objects / models and add `SynchronizedAttribute` for automatic sync, or call a router/synchronizer's send method manually.
Delta-detection engine for `ISynchronizedEntity` objects: compares the current `SyncedAttribute` property values with the last values recorded for a key and reports what changed.

Sends the changed properties of an `ISynchronizedEntity` to clients (delta sync). Available through `Synchronize`. The working implementation comes with the gaming module (registered when `altruist:game` is configured); without it the default implementation throws.

Placeholder `IClientSynchronizator` registered when only the transport is configured. Throws `NotImplementedException`; enable the gaming module (`altruist:game`) for the working implementation. Steps aside when the gaming implementation was registered first, so assembly scan order can't let it win.

Generic entity state-sync payload (`Sync`): the entity's type name plus a property-name → value map of what changed. Sent by the framework's entity sync/broadcast paths; the dictionary values are serialized as untyped objects, so prefer a dedicated packet type for high-frequency or size-sensitive state.

services.summary: Placeholder `IClientSynchronizator` registered when only the transport is configured. Throws `NotImplementedException`; enable the gaming module (`altruist:game`) for the working implementation. Steps aside when the gaming implementation was registered first, so assembly scan order can't let it win.

attributes.summary: Marks a public instance property of an `ISynchronizedEntity` as part of its network-synchronized surface. Only properties carrying this attribute are diffed by `GetSyncChanges` and sent in delta sync packets.

Marks an ISynchronizedEntity class for automatic delta synchronization. Altruist discovers all world objects with this attribute and broadcasts [Synced] property changes automatically — no manual code needed. Default: syncs every world step. A frequency is read in `Ticks` unless a unit is given. Usage: [Synchronized] // sync every step [Synchronized(10)] // sync every 10th step [Synchronized(10, SyncUnit.Hz)] // sync 10 times per second [Synchronized(1, SyncUnit.Seconds)] // sync once per second

spec.name: snapshots
spec.title: Snapshot schemas
spec.summary: A way to declare once in C# how a fast-changing state row (a float array with no field names) is laid out. The same declaration builds the server's allocation-free encoder and exports a JSON schema for the clients' decoders.
use: When you send numeric state of many objects every tick (players, projectiles, match clock) as compact MessagePack rows.
When the server and several clients must agree on what each position of a row means.
avoid: When only changed properties should travel, use entity-sync instead.
When messages are rare or hold names, lists and nested objects, use a plain packet (packets-and-codecs) instead.

keyTypes.summary: Entry points for `SnapshotRowSchema`: `For` declares a row in code (computed values, several views of one type, state classes you do not want to annotate); `FromAttributes` builds one from `SnapshotFieldAttribute`s on the state class itself (plain fields / properties, the declaration sits next to the data).

A declarative, positional snapshot row: the ordered list of values a server writes for one object of type T (a player, a ball, the match clock...) as a `float[]`, which MessagePack sends as a compact array (no names on the wire). The same declaration exports to JSON (`ToJson`) so a client decodes rows by name with `@altruist/net` instead of hand-written indexes: a field is declared once. Encoding runs a delegate compiled once from the field expressions (no reflection, no boxing per call). `Encode` allocates nothing; `Encode` allocates only the row. It is a pure read of T: deterministic, same bits as writing the casts by hand. Use it for state that is sent often as numbers (per-tick snapshots of many objects). Use a plain MessagePack packet with `[Key]` members for rare, mixed-type messages (strings, nested objects), and Altruist's `SyncedAttribute` entity sync for change-tracked world entities where only changed properties should travel. Compatibility: append new fields at the end with a `whenMissing` value so older writers' shorter rows still decode; never reorder or remove fields (indexes are the wire contract).

The snapshot rows and packets a server sends, exported as one JSON document (format `Format`) that client decoders read (`@altruist/net`: `SnapshotSchema`). Commit the JSON next to the client and guard it with a test (`IsCurrent`): the C# declarations stay the single source, and a stale file fails the build instead of desyncing.
Non-generic view of a `SnapshotRowSchema` (export, validation, tooling).
One slot of a `SnapshotRowSchema`: its wire name, position and kind. Read it to document or export a schema; it is created by `SnapshotRowBuilder` or `SnapshotFieldAttribute`, never by hand.

attributes.summary: Marks a public field or property as one slot of a positional snapshot row built with `FromAttributes`. Use it on plain state classes whose members are the values to send; use `For` for computed values. Unrelated to `SyncedAttribute` (named, change-tracked entity sync).

Describes one member of a MessagePack packet (a `[Key(n)]` property) for the snapshot schema export: what the member holds and what a decoder uses when an older writer's packet array ends before it. Needed only on members that hold schema rows or that were appended after a release; other `[Key]` members export as plain values under their camelCase name. Changes nothing about how MessagePack encodes the packet.

spec.name: pairing
spec.title: Device pairing
spec.summary: Lets two devices find each other through the server: a host (for example the game on a TV) opens a session and shows a short code, and companions (phones) join with that code. The server then relays small payloads between them, such as controller input or WebRTC signalling.
use: When a phone should act as a controller or second screen for a game on another device.
When you need to signal a peer-to-peer (WebRTC) link between two devices.
avoid: When you need accounts or secure identity, use the security capabilities. Companions need only the code.
When the devices may reach different server nodes. Sessions live in one process only.

keyTypes.summary: Device pairing over a portal: a host opens a session (`pair-host`) and shows its code; companions join with it (`pair-join`); both send each other opaque payloads (`pair-send`), which the server relays, and keep the connection alive with `pair-ping`. Use it to pair a phone with the game on a TV as a controller, a second screen, or to signal a peer-to-peer (WebRTC) link between them that then bypasses the server.

Device pairing sessions: a host (e.g. the game on a TV) opens a session and gets a short code; companions (e.g. phones used as controllers) join with the code and get a slot; the session relays payloads between the host (slot 0) and its companions. Closing the host closes the session. Pure bookkeeping, no I/O: `PairingPortal` wires it to connections.
Limits of device pairing (`PairingSessions`, `PairingPortal`).
Client request to open a pairing session as its host (gate `pair-host`).
Client request to join a session as a companion (gate `pair-join`).
Client payload for a peer of its session (gate `pair-send`): host to a companion, or a companion to the host.

services.summary: Device pairing sessions: a host (e.g. the game on a TV) opens a session and gets a short code; companions (e.g. phones used as controllers) join with the code and get a slot; the session relays payloads between the host (slot 0) and its companions. Closing the host closes the session. Pure bookkeeping, no I/O: `PairingPortal` wires it to connections.

spec.name: http-api
spec.title: HTTP API
spec.summary: The HTTP side of the server: host, port and path of the ASP.NET Core app, plus what a public API needs. That is one error format, hardening (forwarded headers, security headers, body limits), named rate-limit policies that work across a fleet, and token-guarded access to the dashboard.
use: When you set the HTTP host, port or base path.
When you harden a public API (security headers, HSTS, body size) or rate-limit controllers with [RateLimit("policy")].
avoid: When you limit packets on portals (WebSocket, TCP, UDP), use rate-limit instead.
When you need real-time messages, use portals-and-routing instead.
spec.example:
```yaml
altruist:
  server:
    http:
      host: 0.0.0.0
      port: 8080
      errors:
        format: simple
      hardening:
        security-headers: { enabled: true }
      rate-limit:
        policies:
          api: { permit: 600, window-seconds: 60, path: /api }
```

```csharp
using Altruist.Http;

if (await accounts.ExistsAsync(name))
    throw new HttpApiException(409, "username_taken", "That username is taken.", field: "username");
```

keyTypes.summary: An expected, user-facing failure of an HTTP API call. With `altruist:server:http:errors:format: simple` it is answered with `Status` and the body `{error, message, field?}` (and a `Retry-After` header when `RetryAfterSeconds` is set). The message is shown to the client: never put internals in it.
The HTTP API settings: `HttpErrorOptions`, `HttpHardeningOptions` and `HttpRateLimitOptions`.
Writes error responses in the configured `HttpErrorFormat`.

`altruist:server:http:hardening`: HTTP hardening, every part off unless configured. `server-header` (true): false drops Kestrel's `Server` header.`max-body-bytes`: Kestrel's request body limit for every request (Kestrel's default: 30 MB).`forwarded-headers`: `enabled`, `forward-limit` (1), `known-proxies` (addresses; default loopback only): `X-Forwarded-For` / `-Proto` from trusted proxies set the client address and scheme.`security-headers`: `enabled` (nosniff, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`) and `hsts-max-age-seconds` (HSTS on HTTPS requests; 0 = none).`api`: for requests under `path`, a `content-security-policy`, `no-store` (`Cache-Control`) and `max-body-bytes` (larger bodies are answered 413 `payload_too_large`). The middleware runs first in the pipeline (before the fleet relay, routing and authentication), in this order: forwarded headers, response headers, path rate limits (`HttpRateLimitOptions`), API body limit.
One named limit: at most `Permit` hits per `Window` and partition.

The named HTTP rate limits of `HttpRateLimitOptions`. `[RateLimit("name")]` and path policies use it; call it yourself where a limit must apply after your own checks (e.g. the domain errors of a request win over its limit).

services.summary: Registers the HTTP API features of `altruist:server:http` (`errors`, `hardening`, `rate-limit`). Nothing changes for an app that configures none of them; the server adds the middleware with `UseAltruistHttpHardening`.

The default `IRequestRateLimiter`: sliding windows in memory, or fixed windows in the fleet backplane with `store: backplane` (one limit across every server; memory while the backplane is unreachable or not shared).

spec.name: accounts-and-auth
spec.title: Accounts and Authentication
spec.summary: Everything for signing players in: BCrypt password hashing, HS256 JWT access tokens, rotating refresh tokens in an HttpOnly cookie, one-time tokens (email verification, password reset), session tokens for sockets, and the [Shield] attributes that protect portals and controllers on every transport. Altruist keeps the security-sensitive parts and leaves your account model to you.
use: When players must log in and you want signed access tokens, refresh tokens that detect stolen sessions, and password hashing that is already done right.
When a portal (WebSocket, TCP or UDP) or an HTTP controller must only be reachable by authenticated clients ([JwtShield], [SessionShield], [Shield(typeof(...))]).
When you need email verification or password reset links (one-time tokens) or a custom IShieldAuth such as an API key check.
When you want a ready login controller to extend (JwtAuthController gives signup, login, refresh and upgrade endpoints).
avoid: When a browser must open a WebSocket and cannot set an Authorization header, use connection-tickets instead of putting the token in the URL.
When you need to slow down password guessing or sign-up bots, add abuse-protection (lockout and captcha) on top.
When you only need request throttling, use the HTTP and socket rate limits of the networking capabilities, not auth.
spec.example:
Safe by default: tokens are HS256 only and need an expiry; passwords use BCrypt (work factor 11); the refresh
token lives in an HttpOnly cookie and only its SHA-256 is stored. Not safe by default: if `key` is unset Altruist
uses a PUBLIC development key. In Production an app with an `altruist:security` section refuses to start when the
key is unset, is the development key, or is shorter than `min-key-bytes` (32 bytes). Set the key from the
environment, for example `ALTRUIST__SECURITY__KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 48)`.
Pick `password:prehash` before you store hashes: hashes of the two modes do not verify against each other.
```yaml
altruist:
  security:
    mode: jwt                  # jwt (default) | session
    key: ""                    # set from ALTRUIST__SECURITY__KEY, never commit it
    min-key-bytes: 32          # shorter keys are refused in Production
    access-token-minutes: 15
    password:
      work-factor: 11          # BCrypt cost, 4-31
      prehash: none            # none | sha384 (sha384 stops the 72-byte BCrypt truncation)
    refresh-tokens:
      lifetime-days: 30
      max-sessions: 10
    refresh-cookie:
      same-site: strict        # strict | lax | none
```
```csharp
[Vault("refresh_tokens", Keyspace: "myapp")]
public sealed class RefreshTokenVault : RefreshTokenModel { }

[ApiController, Route("auth")]
public sealed class AuthController(
    IRefreshTokenService refresh, IAccessTokenIssuer access, RefreshCookie cookie, Accounts accounts) : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpPost("login")]
    public async Task<IActionResult> Login(LoginRequest body, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var account = await accounts.VerifyAsync(body.Username, body.Password, ct);
        if (account is null) return Unauthorized();
        cookie.Append(Response, await refresh.IssueAsync(account.Id, ct: ct));
        return Ok(new { accessToken = access.Issue(account.Id).Token });
    }
}

[Portal("/game")]
[JwtShield]
public class SecureGamePortal : AltruistPortal { }
```

keyTypes.summary: JWT bearer authentication (`altruist:security:mode: jwt`, the default) with the HS256 key `altruist:security:key`. Tokens must be HS256-signed and carry an expiry. Key guard: in Production (`AltruistEnvironment`) an application with an `altruist:security` section refuses to start when the key is the built-in development key, unset, or shorter than `altruist:security:min-key-bytes` (default 32); other environments log a warning. Options under `altruist:security:jwt`: `map-inbound-claims` (ASP.NET maps `sub` to `NameIdentifier` and so on; default true) and `name-claim` (the claim `User.Identity.Name` reads). Tokens are validated with issuer and audience `Altruist`, zero clock skew, and must not be expired. The `SymmetricSecurityKey` and `TokenValidationParameters` are registered as singletons so token issuers can sign with the same key. `mode: session` registers nothing here (session auth is handled elsewhere); any other non-empty mode logs a warning and configures no authentication.

Password hashing for account stores. Inject it in your `ILoginService`: store `Hash` results and check sign-ins with `Verify`. Default: `BcryptPasswordHasher` (singleton). Not for tokens: opaque tokens are hashed with `Hash` (fast SHA-256 suffices for 256-bit random secrets).

Issues short-lived JWT access tokens that the JWT bearer setup of `AuthConfiguration` validates (same key, issuer and audience). Stateless and safe to share: every call gets its own claims. Pair it with `IRefreshTokenService` for sessions that outlive the token. Registered (singleton) only with `altruist:security:mode: jwt` (the default mode).

Rotating refresh tokens with reuse detection. Each sign-in starts a family; every refresh consumes the presented token and issues its successor in the same family. Presenting a token that was already rotated revokes the family (the attacker's and the victim's sessions end). Only hashes are stored, in the `RefreshTokenModel` table. Every call joins the ambient SQL transaction (`ISqlTransactionProvider`), so a sign-in can create the account and its first token atomically.

The refresh token as an HttpOnly cookie, out of reach of page scripts. Config `altruist:security:refresh-cookie`: `name` ("refresh_token"), `path` (the auth routes that read it, "/"), `same-site` (strict | lax | none; "strict"), `csrf-header` ("X-Requested-With") and `csrf-value` ("1"). The cookie is `Secure` on HTTPS requests (`IsHttps`, which honours forwarded headers). Endpoints authenticated by the cookie must check `HasCsrfHeader`: cross-site forms cannot send a custom header, and cross-origin scripts would need a CORS preflight.
Single-use tokens stored hashed in SQL. Every call joins the ambient SQL transaction, so consuming a token and acting on it (e.g. marking an email verified) commit or roll back together.
Extends `AuthController` to implement JWT-specific login, refresh handling, and a session upgrade flow using `IAuthService` (HTTP version of AuthPortal).
An authentication handler run by `ShieldAttribute` for guarded MVC actions, WebSocket portals and TCP/UDP connections.

services.summary: The default `IAccessTokenIssuer`: signs with the `TokenValidationParameters` registered by `AuthConfiguration` (`altruist:security:mode: jwt`). Config `altruist:security:access-token-minutes` (default 15).

JWT bearer authentication (`altruist:security:mode: jwt`, the default) with the HS256 key `altruist:security:key`. Tokens must be HS256-signed and carry an expiry. Key guard: in Production (`AltruistEnvironment`) an application with an `altruist:security` section refuses to start when the key is the built-in development key, unset, or shorter than `altruist:security:min-key-bytes` (default 32); other environments log a warning. Options under `altruist:security:jwt`: `map-inbound-claims` (ASP.NET maps `sub` to `NameIdentifier` and so on; default true) and `name-claim` (the claim `User.Identity.Name` reads). Tokens are validated with issuer and audience `Altruist`, zero clock skew, and must not be expired. The `SymmetricSecurityKey` and `TokenValidationParameters` are registered as singletons so token issuers can sign with the same key. `mode: session` registers nothing here (session auth is handled elsewhere); any other non-empty mode logs a warning and configures no authentication.

BCrypt password hashes. Config `altruist:security:password`: `work-factor` (default 11) and `prehash`: `none` (default, plain BCrypt, which only uses the first 72 bytes of a password) or `sha384` (BCrypt over a SHA-384 pre-hash, BCrypt.Net's "enhanced" mode, so long passwords are not truncated). Hashes of one prehash mode do not verify in the other: pick it before storing hashes.

The `IShieldAuth` behind `JwtShieldAttribute` (registered with `altruist:security:mode: jwt`). Reads the bearer JWT (an optional `;jwt` suffix is ignored), validates it with `IJwtTokenValidator`, sets `HttpContext.User` for HTTP and returns `AuthDetails` whose principal is the `sub` claim and whose lifetime is the token's.

Default `IJwtTokenIssuer` (singleton when `altruist:security` exists). The access JWT lives `altruist:security:jwt:access-token-minutes` (default 60) and the refresh JWT `altruist:security:jwt:refresh-token-minutes` (default 10080, 7 days; `SetRefreshTokenExpiry` overrides it per copy). Both carry the same claims plus a random `jti` and get a `;jwt` suffix; the issued `AccessExpiration` and `RefreshExpiration` match their `exp`. Call `WithClaims` per request: it returns a copy, so the shared singleton is never mutated with a caller's claims.

Default `IJwtTokenValidator` and `ITokenValidator` in `altruist:security:mode: jwt`: validates signature (HS256), issuer, audience and lifetime (no clock skew) with the registered `TokenValidationParameters`.

Default `IJwtTokenValidator` and `ITokenValidator` in `altruist:security:mode: jwt`: validates signature (HS256), issuer, audience and lifetime (no clock skew) with the registered `TokenValidationParameters`.

The refresh token as an HttpOnly cookie, out of reach of page scripts. Config `altruist:security:refresh-cookie`: `name` ("refresh_token"), `path` (the auth routes that read it, "/"), `same-site` (strict | lax | none; "strict"), `csrf-header` ("X-Requested-With") and `csrf-value` ("1"). The cookie is `Secure` on HTTPS requests (`IsHttps`, which honours forwarded headers). Endpoints authenticated by the cookie must check `HasCsrfHeader`: cross-site forms cannot send a custom header, and cross-origin scripts would need a CORS preflight.

The `IShieldAuth` behind `SessionShieldAttribute` (registered with `altruist:security:mode: session`). Looks the token up with `FindByTokenAsync` (in whichever group it was saved under), requires an unexpired access time and a matching client IP, and keeps a process-wide copy for `CacheValidationInterval` before reading the store again. A session stays valid until its issued `AccessExpiration`; validation never changes it.
Default `ISessionTokenIssuer`: access tokens valid 1 hour and refresh tokens 7 days unless other lifetimes are passed to the constructor.
Default `ISessionTokenValidator` (when `altruist:security` exists).
Session-token cache wrapper. Reads/writes `AuthTokenSessionModel` against the in-memory `ICacheProvider`, dual-writing to the optional vault when configured.

Registers the SQL token stores for the token vaults the application declares: an `IRefreshTokenService` for each `RefreshTokenModel` vault and an `IOneTimeTokenStore` for each `OneTimeTokenModel` vault (also as `IRefreshTokenService` / `IOneTimeTokenStore` when there is exactly one of the kind), and the `TokenPruneService` that cleans them up. Nothing is registered for applications without such vaults.
Default `IAuthService` (registered when `altruist:security` exists). Validates with the registered `ITokenValidator` (JWT in `mode: jwt`). Override `Upgrade` to customise.

config.description: Access JWT lifetime in minutes; must be positive.
Refresh JWT lifetime in minutes; must be longer than the access lifetime.

attributes.summary: Requires a valid JWT in `Authorization: Bearer ...` (via `JwtAuth`); otherwise 401. Needs `altruist:security:mode: jwt` (the default). Use on controllers, actions and portals reached over HTTP or a WebSocket upgrade by clients that can send headers; browsers opening WebSockets should use `TicketShieldAttribute` instead. Plain ASP.NET `[Authorize]` works too for MVC.

Requires a valid server-side session token (via `SessionTokenAuth`, registered with `altruist:security:mode: session`); otherwise 401. The token is read from the context's `Token` (for HTTP the `Authorization: Bearer` credential) and the session must be bound to the caller's IP. For JWT mode use `JwtShieldAttribute`; for browser WebSockets use `TicketShieldAttribute`.

Guards an MVC controller/action or a portal with an `IShieldAuth` handler: the request (or WebSocket upgrade) gets 401 unless the handler succeeds. On success the `AuthResult` is stored in `HttpContext.Items["AuthResult"]`. Fails closed: a handler that cannot be resolved or throws denies.
